methodologies.title: Web Application & API Penetration Testing
methodologies.summary: A phased, OWASP-WSTG-aligned methodology for assessing the security of web applications and their APIs on authorized engagements — from passive reconnaissance through input-validation, authentication/authorization, session, business-logic and API testing, each step paired with the detection and mitigation guidance a defender needs.
methodologies.authorization_note: Run only against applications you own or are explicitly authorized to assess. In AEGIS, active probing of a live web target is gated by the fail-closed authorization scope (aegis/core/authorization.py); passive steps reason over the declared attack-surface inventory.

references.owasp_wstg: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide v4.2

phases.name: Reconnaissance & Information Gathering
phases.goal: Map the application surface, technologies, and entry points before any active test.

techniques.name: Passive surface & fingerprinting
techniques.objective: Enumerate hosts, subdomains, technologies, and framework/version disclosure without touching sensitive functionality.
techniques.approach: Review declared endpoints/OpenAPI/GraphQL schema; correlate response headers, error pages, and public metadata to fingerprint the stack.
detection: Alert on scanning bursts and 404 walks
Monitor for enumeration of well-known paths

techniques.name: Configuration & deployment review
techniques.objective: Identify insecure platform/config: default files, exposed admin, TLS posture, security headers, CORS.
techniques.approach: Inspect TLS configuration, HTTP security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options), CORS policy, and cookie flags against ASVS baselines.
detection: Continuous header/TLS posture monitoring
Config drift detection in CI
mitigations: Enforce security headers at the edge

phases.name: Identity, Authentication & Session Management
phases.goal: Verify that users are authenticated robustly and sessions cannot be hijacked or fixed.

techniques.name: Authentication robustness
techniques.objective: Assess resistance to credential stuffing, brute force, weak password policy, and username enumeration.
techniques.approach: Measure lockout/rate-limit behaviour, response-timing/message differences between valid and invalid users, and MFA enforcement — using benign, authorized test accounts.
signals: No lockout or rate limiting on login
Distinct error for valid vs invalid usernames
detection: Alert on failed-login spikes per account/IP
Detect impossible-travel and credential-stuffing patterns
mitigations: Enforce MFA and strong password policy

techniques.name: Session management
techniques.objective: Verify session tokens are unpredictable, rotated on privilege change, invalidated on logout, and protected in transit.
techniques.approach: Analyze token entropy/scope, fixation resistance (rotation on login), logout/idle-timeout invalidation, and cookie transport flags.
signals: Session id not rotated after login (fixation)
detection: Track concurrent sessions per principal
Alert on session reuse from new geo/device

phases.name: Authorization
phases.goal: Confirm access controls enforce least privilege across objects and functions.

techniques.name: Broken object/function level authorization (BOLA/BFLA)
techniques.objective: Detect horizontal and vertical privilege escalation: accessing other users' objects or admin functions.
techniques.approach: With two authorized low-privilege test principals, verify that object identifiers and privileged functions are enforced server-side, not by client-side controls.
signals: Object accessible by changing an id (IDOR)
Admin function reachable by a normal user
detection: Log and alert on cross-tenant object access
Monitor privileged-endpoint calls by role

phases.name: Input Validation & Injection
phases.goal: Determine whether untrusted input can alter query, command, markup, or template semantics.

techniques.name: Injection (SQL/NoSQL/command/template)
techniques.objective: Assess whether user input crosses a code/data boundary in queries, OS commands, or template engines.
techniques.approach: Send benign, non-destructive marker inputs to observe differential responses and error behaviour; confirm findings only via the authorized controlled-validation path — never destructive payloads.
signals: Database/SQL errors reflected to the client
detection: WAF/RASP alerts on injection patterns
Log query errors and anomalous query shapes
mitigations: Least-privilege DB accounts; disable dangerous template features

techniques.name: Cross-site scripting (reflected/stored/DOM)
techniques.objective: Assess whether input is rendered into a browser context without correct encoding, enabling script execution.
techniques.approach: Inject benign, non-persistent markers into reflected and DOM sinks under authorization; review CSP and output-encoding of each sink.
signals: Input reflected unencoded into HTML/JS/attribute context
DOM sink writes location/innerHTML from input
detection: CSP violation reporting
Alert on script-like input in stored fields

techniques.name: Server-side request forgery (SSRF)
techniques.objective: Determine whether the server can be coerced into making attacker-controlled requests (e.g., to cloud metadata or internal services).
techniques.approach: Review URL/host-taking parameters and their egress controls; validate only against authorized, non-production endpoints.
detection: Egress monitoring for internal/metadata destinations
Alert on outbound requests from app tier to RFC1918/link-local
mitigations: Egress allow-list and metadata endpoint blocking
Use IMDSv2 / hop-limit on cloud metadata

phases.name: Business Logic & API Security
phases.goal: Test workflow integrity and API-specific weaknesses beyond generic injection.

techniques.name: Business-logic & workflow abuse
techniques.objective: Identify flows that can be replayed, reordered, or manipulated (price/quantity tampering, race conditions, insufficient limits).
techniques.approach: Model the intended state machine and test for skipped/duplicated steps and value tampering with authorized accounts.
detection: Anomaly detection on transaction sequences
Idempotency and rate monitoring

owasp_api: API6:2023 Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows

techniques.name: Unrestricted resource consumption & rate limiting
techniques.objective: Determine whether expensive or state-changing endpoints (including AI/inference) enforce authentication and rate/quota limits.
techniques.approach: Review declared endpoints for auth requirement and rate-limit metadata; measure quota enforcement on authorized test traffic.
signals: No rate limit on costly operation
detection: Per-principal quota and cost monitoring
Alert on volume/cost spikes

phases.name: Analysis, Evidence & Reporting
phases.goal: Turn measured weaknesses into reproducible, standards-mapped findings with remediation.

techniques.name: Evidence collection & standards mapping
techniques.objective: Record reproducible evidence for each finding and map it to OWASP/ASVS/ATT&CK with severity and confidence.
techniques.approach: Capture request/response transcripts and reproduction metadata; derive severity from measured impact × confidence, and attach mitigation + regression tests.
detection: N/A (reporting discipline)
mitigations: Track each finding to a regression test
Re-test after remediation to confirm closure

owasp_asvs: V1 Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling

methodologies.title: Active Directory Security Assessment
methodologies.summary: An assumed-breach, ATT&CK-aligned methodology for assessing Active Directory: discovery and enumeration, credential-access exposure, lateral-movement paths, privilege-escalation and domain-dominance conditions, and persistence — each paired with the Windows detection telemetry and hardening control that closes it.
methodologies.authorization_note: Run only inside a directory you own or are explicitly authorized to assess (signed rules of engagement). Prefer a lab or an isolated, monitored assessment window; coordinate with the blue team so detections can be validated. In AEGIS, hosts/scopes are enforced fail-closed and active checks run only through the controlled-validation path.

references.ms_hardening: Microsoft Securing Active Directory / Tiered Admin model

phases.name: Discovery & Enumeration
phases.goal: Build an accurate model of the domain: principals, groups, trusts, and privileged relationships.

techniques.name: Domain, user, and group enumeration
techniques.objective: Inventory domain objects, group memberships, GPOs, and trusts to map the identity terrain (typically via authenticated LDAP as any domain user).
techniques.approach: Query directory objects and build a relationship graph (users→groups→rights→hosts) to identify privileged principals and attack paths; read-only.
detection: Monitor bulk/anomalous LDAP queries (event 1644 with diagnostics)
Alert on directory enumeration from non-admin hosts
mitigations: Restrict who can enumerate sensitive attributes
Deploy AD tiering to limit blast radius

techniques.name: Attack-path / ACL relationship analysis
techniques.objective: Identify dangerous ACLs and delegation (GenericAll, WriteDACL, GenericWrite, constrained/unconstrained delegation) that form escalation edges to Domain Admin.
techniques.approach: Analyze object ACLs and delegation settings to compute shortest privileged paths; purely analytical over collected relationship data.
signals: Users with WriteDACL over privileged objects
detection: Baseline and alert on ACL changes to privileged objects (event 5136)
Flag new delegation configuration
mitigations: Remove unnecessary ACEs; enforce least privilege on AD objects
Mark privileged accounts 'sensitive, cannot be delegated'
Prefer constrained delegation with protocol transition scrutiny

phases.name: Credential Access Exposure
phases.goal: Determine whether credential material can be obtained from Kerberos, the directory, or endpoints.

techniques.name: Kerberoasting exposure (service-account SPNs)
techniques.objective: Assess whether service accounts with SPNs use weak, crackable passwords, allowing offline recovery of service-ticket-encrypted credentials.
techniques.approach: Inventory accounts with SPNs and evaluate password strength/rotation policy and encryption type; treat any offline validation as authorized and isolated.
signals: Service accounts with SPNs and weak/never-expiring passwords
detection: Alert on abnormal volume of Kerberos TGS requests (event 4769), especially RC4
Baseline per-account service-ticket request rates
mitigations: Use group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) with long random passwords
Keep service accounts out of privileged groups

techniques.name: AS-REP roasting exposure (pre-auth disabled)
techniques.objective: Identify accounts with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled, whose AS-REP can be recovered offline.
techniques.approach: Enumerate accounts with 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' set; report as configuration weakness.
signals: Such accounts also privileged or with weak passwords
detection: Alert on AS-REQ without pre-auth (event 4768 with pre-auth type 0)
Inventory pre-auth-disabled accounts continuously
mitigations: Require Kerberos pre-authentication for all accounts

techniques.name: Endpoint credential-material exposure
techniques.objective: Assess exposure of cached credentials, tokens, and secrets on endpoints (LSASS memory, credential caches, SYSVOL scripts/GPP).
techniques.approach: Review protections (Credential Guard, LSASS protection, RunAsPPL) and scan SYSVOL/scripts for embedded secrets; read-only configuration review.
detection: Alert on LSASS access by non-system processes (Sysmon event 10)
Monitor SYSVOL for secrets
mitigations: Deploy LAPS for unique local-admin passwords
Remove secrets from SYSVOL; migrate off GPP passwords

phases.name: Lateral Movement
phases.goal: Evaluate whether obtained credentials/tickets enable movement between hosts.

techniques.name: Credential-reuse & ticket-based movement
techniques.objective: Determine whether hash/ticket reuse (pass-the-hash / pass-the-ticket) or over-broad local-admin rights allow lateral movement.
techniques.approach: Map where each principal has local-admin rights and whether NTLM/Kerberos reuse is constrained; validate only against authorized hosts.
detection: Alert on lateral auth patterns (event 4624 type 3/10 from unusual sources)
Detect anomalous admin logons and remote-service creation (event 7045)
mitigations: Windows Defender Credential Guard; restrict NTLM

phases.name: Privilege Escalation & Domain Dominance
phases.goal: Identify conditions that grant domain-wide control.

techniques.name: Directory-replication (DCSync) rights exposure
techniques.objective: Assess whether non-DC principals hold replication rights (Replicating Directory Changes / All) enabling secret extraction of any account.
techniques.approach: Audit which principals hold DS-Replication-Get-Changes[-All] on the domain head; report over-grants as critical.
detection: Alert on replication requests from non-DC sources (event 4662 with the replication GUIDs)
Baseline expected replication partners
mitigations: Remove replication rights from non-DC principals
Restrict to domain controllers only; monitor tightly

techniques.name: AD Certificate Services (AD CS) misconfiguration
techniques.objective: Identify vulnerable certificate templates / CA settings that permit authentication-capable certificate issuance for arbitrary principals.
techniques.approach: Enumerate templates and CA flags for enrollee-supplied SAN, dangerous EKUs, and weak enrollment ACLs; analytical review of PKI configuration.
signals: Templates allowing requester-supplied SAN with client-auth EKU
detection: Monitor certificate issuance (event 4886/4887) for anomalous SANs
Alert on certificate-based logons for sensitive accounts
mitigations: Remove enrollee-supplied SAN; require manager approval
Disable dangerous CA flags; enable CA auditing

mitre_attack: T1649 Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates

phases.name: Persistence & Defense Validation
phases.goal: Assess durable-access conditions and validate that detections/hardening are effective.

techniques.name: Persistence-condition & Tier-0 integrity review
techniques.objective: Identify conditions enabling durable domain access (e.g., forged-ticket exposure via krbtgt hygiene, rogue trusts, GPO abuse) and verify Tier-0 isolation.
techniques.approach: Review krbtgt rotation cadence, trust configuration, GPO edit rights, and Tier-0 separation; recommend detections and drills rather than establishing persistence.
detection: Monitor GPO changes (event 5136 on GPC objects)
Alert on TGT lifetimes/anomalies; watch for golden/silver-ticket indicators
mitigations: Rotate krbtgt twice on schedule and after compromise
Enforce Tier-0 admin isolation and PAWs
Restrict and monitor GPO edit rights and trusts

methodologies.title: AI / LLM / Agentic Red-Teaming
methodologies.summary: A phased methodology for adversarial evaluation of AI systems — LLMs, RAG pipelines, and agentic/MCP surfaces — spanning threat modeling, attack-surface mapping, adversarial execution (prompt injection, jailbreak, tool/agent abuse, RAG poisoning, multimodal), evidence-based scoring, and remediation. It is the human-readable companion to AEGIS's adaptive evaluation loop and 23-agent collective.
methodologies.authorization_note: Assess only AI systems you own or are explicitly authorized to evaluate. AEGIS routes every provider request through the fail-closed authorization scope; the mutation framework produces semantics-preserving re-encodings to measure robustness and calibration, not to defeat safety controls.

references.redamon: redamon autonomous pipeline (samugit83/redamon) — pipeline shape only

phases.name: Planning & Threat Modeling
phases.goal: Define scope, objectives, risk profile, and rules of engagement before probing.

techniques.name: Threat modeling & scoping
techniques.objective: Enumerate assets, trust boundaries, and abuse cases for the AI system; set measurable objectives and an authorized scope.
techniques.approach: Map data flows (prompt, context, tools, memory, outputs), identify actors and boundaries, and record a signed scope with volume/time caps.
signals: No defined abuse cases or success criteria
detection: N/A (governance activity)
mitigations: Maintain an AI system card and data-flow diagram

phases.name: Reconnaissance & Attack-Surface Mapping
phases.goal: Discover and characterise the AI surface: models, RAG stores, tools, agents, and exposed endpoints.

techniques.name: AI attack-surface detection
techniques.objective: Identify inference endpoints, RAG retrieval, MCP tools/resources, and agent autonomy, and flag those that are unauthenticated or unbounded.
techniques.approach: Enumerate declared surface inventory and characterise capabilities/boundaries with benign probes (AEGIS capability/boundary/recon agents).
detection: Inventory and monitor AI endpoints and tool grants
Alert on unauthenticated inference traffic

phases.name: Adversarial Execution
phases.goal: Probe model, RAG, and agent behaviour with reproducible, semantics-preserving adversarial inputs.

techniques.name: Prompt injection & instruction-hierarchy testing
techniques.objective: Measure susceptibility to direct and indirect prompt injection and to instruction-hierarchy override (system vs. user vs. tool content).
techniques.approach: Apply reproducible mutation transforms and layered-instruction probes; score whether untrusted content can override authoritative instructions.
detection: Log and review tool/RAG content that alters behaviour
Output/action policy checks with anomaly alerting
mitigations: Strong instruction hierarchy and content provenance separation

techniques.name: Agentic / tool-abuse & excessive-agency testing
techniques.objective: Determine whether an agent can be steered to misuse tools, exceed authority, or chain actions toward a harmful goal.
techniques.approach: Exercise agent tool-use under authorized scenarios; check confirmation gates, scope enforcement, and goal-hijack resistance.
detection: Audit tool-call chains; alert on dangerous tool use
Rate/scope monitoring per agent identity

techniques.name: RAG grounding & poisoning testing
techniques.objective: Assess grounding rate, unsupported-citation behaviour, and susceptibility to retrieval/context poisoning.
techniques.approach: Probe with queries whose ground truth is known; measure grounding, source attribution, and behaviour on adversarial/poisoned context.
detection: Track grounding/attribution metrics in production
Content integrity checks on the vector store
mitigations: Provenance and integrity controls on the corpus
Grounding/citation verification; refusal on low support

techniques.name: Robustness, calibration & sensitive-data-exposure testing
techniques.objective: Measure output stability under benign re-encoding, confidence calibration, and resistance to training/system-data disclosure.
techniques.approach: Apply semantics-preserving transforms (Unicode/encoding/format) and consistency/calibration probes; test for system-prompt or sensitive-data leakage.
detection: Monitor answer variance and refusal patterns
DLP on model outputs

phases.name: Evaluation & Scoring
phases.goal: Quantify results with reproducible, statistically grounded metrics.

techniques.name: Attack-success-rate & confidence scoring
techniques.objective: Compute per-dimension success/failure rates with calibrated confidence and derive severity from measured shortfall × confidence.
techniques.approach: Aggregate probe outcomes into rates with Wilson-interval confidence (AEGIS metrics/confidence); require minimum sample sizes before rating.
signals: Severity not tied to measured impact
detection: N/A (measurement discipline)
mitigations: Report confidence bands and sample sizes
Set fail-on thresholds for CI gating

phases.name: Reporting & Remediation
phases.goal: Deliver standards-mapped findings, mitigations, and regression tests, then re-test.

techniques.name: Remediation, regression & continuous validation
techniques.objective: Attach mitigation guidance and a regression test to each finding, and re-run to confirm closure and prevent regression.
techniques.approach: Map findings to frameworks, generate mitigations + regression probes, and schedule continuous re-evaluation (AEGIS memory/regression + CI).
signals: Findings without mitigations or regression tests
detection: Track regression suite pass/fail over time
mitigations: Bind every finding to a regression test
Continuous validation in CI with severity gates
